questions.prompt: What are the three main parts of the ear?
questions.explanation: The ear is divided into the outer ear, middle ear, and inner ear, each doing part of the hearing job.
questions.misconception: The ear's three parts are named by depth (outer, middle, inner), not position or kidney-style names.

questions.prompt: What happens when sound waves hit the eardrum?
options: It vibrates and passes the motion to tiny bones
questions.explanation: Sound waves make the thin eardrum vibrate, and those vibrations are passed along by the middle-ear bones.
questions.misconception: The eardrum does not store or block sound - it converts air waves into a mechanical vibration.

questions.prompt: Where are vibrations turned into nerve signals?
questions.explanation: The coiled cochlea in the inner ear turns the vibrations into nerve signals sent to the brain.
questions.misconception: The outer ear and eardrum just move the sound along - the actual signal-making happens in the cochlea.

questions.prompt: Besides hearing, what else does the ear help with?
questions.explanation: The semicircular canals of the inner ear help you keep your balance.
questions.misconception: Taste, smell, and touch are handled by other senses - the ear uniquely adds balance to hearing.

questions.prompt: In what order do vibrations travel in the middle ear?
options: Eardrum, hammer, anvil, stirrup, then cochlea
questions.explanation: The eardrum vibrates, then the three tiny bones - hammer, anvil, stirrup - pass the vibration to the cochlea.
questions.misconception: The three bones have a strict order (hammer, anvil, stirrup) - the chain always runs eardrum to cochlea.
